Finite-interval integer counts identify the reflected radial phase even when
total residual mass is infinite. Monotonicity and mass growth are derived
from the same canonical residual measure. Boundary zeros are retained.

def quantizationResidualCumulative {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (quantizationResidualMeasure hW).real (Ioc 0 (2 * x))

def quantizationOriginPhase {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) : ℂ :=

  ne_top_of_le_ne_top (quantization_boundaryMeasure_Icc_ne_top hW a b)
    ((quantizationResidualMeasure_le hW _).trans (measure_mono Ioc_subset_Icc_self))

theorem monotone_quantizationResidualCumulative {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) :
    Monotone (quantizationResidualCumulative hW) := by
  intro a b hab
  exact ENNReal.toReal_mono (quantizationResidualMeasure_Ioc_ne_top hW 0 (2 * b))
    (measure_mono (by intro x hx; exact ⟨hx.1, by linarith [hx.2]⟩))

      (quantizationResidualMeasure hW).real (Icc (-T) T) ≤ K * T ^ α)
    {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 ≤ x) : quantizationResidualCumulative hW x ≤ (K * 2 ^ α) * x ^ α := by
  have hfin : quantizationResidualMeasure hW (Icc (-(2 * x)) (2 * x)) ≠ ∞ :=
    ne_top_of_le_ne_top (quantization_boundaryMeasure_Icc_ne_top hW (-(2 * x)) (2 * x))
      (quantizationResidualMeasure_le hW _)
  have hsub : Ioc 0 (2 * x) ⊆ Icc (-(2 * x)) (2 * x) := by
    intro r hr; exact ⟨by linarith [hr.1], hr.2⟩
  calc quantizationResidualCumulative hW x ≤
        (quantizationResidualMeasure hW).real (Icc (-(2 * x)) (2 * x)) :=
          ENNReal.toReal_mono hfin (measure_mono hsub)
    _ ≤ K * (2 * x) ^ α := hgrowth _ (by linarith)
    _ = _ := by rw [Real.mul_rpow (by norm_num) (by linarith : 0 ≤ x)]; ring

  have hd : Disjoint (Ioo 0 y) {y} := by

/-!
# Continuity of the actual residual cumulative lift

A locally finite residual measure has atoms below one. Every point therefore
has a surrounding interval of mass below one. Continuity of the exponential
phase forces the monotone cumulative function's two one-sided limits to agree.
This retains singular-continuous mass and derives continuity from the actual
source and its represented phase, without an atomlessness premise.
-/

theorem quantization_exp_phase_eq {u v : ℝ}
    (h : cexp (((2 * Real.pi * u : ℝ) : ℂ) * I) =
      cexp (((2 * Real.pi * v : ℝ) : ℂ) * I)) : ∃ n : ℤ, u = v + n := by
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := Complex.exp_eq_exp_iff_exists_int.mp h
  have hi := congrArg Complex.im hn
  simp at hi
  refine ⟨n, ?_⟩
  nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]

theorem quantization_continuousAt_of_phase {C : ℝ → ℝ} (hC : Monotone C)
    {a x b : ℝ} (ha : a < x) (hb : x < b) (hsmall : C b - C a < 1)
    (hphase : ContinuousAt (fun y => cexp (((2 * Real.pi * C y : ℝ) : ℂ) * I)) x) :
    ContinuousAt C x := by
  let e : ℝ → ℂ := fun u => cexp (((2 * Real.pi * u : ℝ) : ℂ) * I)
  have he : Continuous e := by fun_prop
  have hl : e (leftLim C x) = e (C x) :=
    tendsto_nhds_unique (he.continuousAt.tendsto.comp (hC.tendsto_leftLim x))
      (hphase.tendsto.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds)
  have hr : e (rightLim C x) = e (C x) :=
    tendsto_nhds_unique (he.continuousAt.tendsto.comp (hC.tendsto_rightLim x))
      (hphase.tendsto.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds)
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := quantization_exp_phase_eq (hr.trans hl.symm)
  have hn0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ n := by linarith [hC.leftLim_le_rightLim (le_refl x)]
  have hn1 : (n : ℝ) < 1 := by linarith [hC.le_leftLim ha, hC.rightLim_le hb]
  have hnz : n = 0 := by
    have : (0 : ℤ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn0
    have : n < (1 : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast hn1
    omega
  apply hC.continuousAt_iff_leftLim_eq_rightLim.mpr
  simpa only [hnz, Int.cast_zero, add_zero] using hn.symm

  have hxb : x < b := by dsimp [b]; linarith
  have hab : 2*a ≤ 2*b := by linarith
  have hadd : ν.real (Ioc 0 (2*b)) = ν.real (Ioc 0 (2*a)) + ν.real (Ioc (2*a) (2*b)) := by
    rw [← Ioc_union_Ioc_eq_Ioc (show 0 ≤ 2*a by positivity) hab]

/-!
# Removing primes destroys Weil positivity

For a set `R` of primes, let `Λ_R(n) = Λ(n)` unless `n` is a power of a prime in `R`, and
`Λ_R(n) = 0` otherwise: the von Mangoldt function of `ζ(s) ∏_{p ∈ R}(1 - p^{-s})`.  Removing finitely
many Euler factors does not move the zeros of `ζ` in the critical strip (the new zeros lie on
`Re s = 0`), but it destroys Weil positivity for the archimedean datum of `ζ`, unconditionally:
`Λ_R ≤ Λ`, and a full-cone Weil-positive minorant of `Λ` equals `Λ`
(`eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_le`).
-/

namespace RHTower
namespace RemovedPrimes

open ArithmeticFunction

/-- The von Mangoldt function with the powers of the primes in `R` removed. -/
noncomputable def vonMangoldtWithout (R : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Set.indicator {m | ¬ ∃ p ∈ R, ∃ k, m = p ^ k} (fun m => (vonMangoldt m : ℝ)) n

theorem vonMangoldtWithout_le (R : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    vonMangoldtWithout R n ≤ (vonMangoldt n : ℝ) :=
  Set.indicator_le_self' (fun _ _ => vonMangoldt_nonneg) n

/-- **Removing any prime destroys Weil positivity.**  If `R` contains a prime, then the von Mangoldt
function with the powers of the primes of `R` removed is not full-cone Weil-positive. -/
theorem not_weilPositiveFull_vonMangoldtWithout {R : Set ℕ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpR : p ∈ R) :
    ¬ WeilPositiveFull (vonMangoldtWithout R) := by
  intro hW
  have h := eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_le hW fun n _ => vonMangoldtWithout_le R n
  have hp2 := h p hp.two_le
  have hmem : p ∉ {m : ℕ | ¬ ∃ q ∈ R, ∃ k, m = q ^ k} := by
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, not_not]
    exact ⟨p, hpR, 1, (pow_one p).symm⟩
  have h0 : vonMangoldtWithout R p = 0 := Set.indicator_of_notMem hmem _
  rw [h0, vonMangoldt_apply_prime hp] at hp2
  exact (Real.log_pos (by exact_mod_cast hp.one_lt)).ne' hp2.symm

/-- In particular, the von Mangoldt function of `(1 - 2^{-s}) ζ(s)` (the prime `2` removed) is not
full-cone Weil-positive. -/
theorem not_weilPositiveFull_without_two :
    ¬ WeilPositiveFull (vonMangoldtWithout {2}) :=
  not_weilPositiveFull_vonMangoldtWithout Nat.prime_two rfl

end RemovedPrimes

/-!
# An integer counting function forces `Λ` and the Riemann hypothesis

Let `lam` be full-cone Weil-positive with boundary measure `μ = μ_lam`.  Suppose its counting
function is integer valued almost everywhere: there is a set `Y` of full Lebesgue measure with
`μ((a,b]) ∈ ℕ` for all `a < b` in `Y`.  Suppose also that `μ` has no mass on `(−1, 1)`.

**Theorem** (`vonMangoldt_and_riemannHypothesis_of_integer_counting`).  Then `lam(n) = Λ(n)` for
every `n ≥ 2`, and the Riemann hypothesis holds.

Along the critical line the cumulative boundary mass `μ((0,t])` is `1/π` times the argument of the
completed exponential `s(s−1)Γ_ℝ(s) exp(Σ lam(n) n^{−s}/log n)`.  The hypothesis therefore says
that this completed exponential has constant phase modulo `π` at almost every point of the line.
No analytic continuation across the line and no regularity of the boundary values are assumed.

**Proof.**
* Integer counting on a dense set isolates every point.  Each `x` has an open interval `I ∋ x`
  with `μ(I ∖ {x}) = 0` and `μ{x} ∈ ℕ` (`exists_isolating_interval`).  Lindelöf's theorem then
  makes the non-atoms `μ`-null and the atoms countable (`atoms_countable_and_compl_null`), so `μ`
  is a countable sum of integer point masses.
* The Weil continuation satisfies `Φ(s̄) = conj Φ(s)` on `Re s > 1/2`.  This holds on `Re s > 1`,

  ordinates `t_j ≥ 1`.  The converse explicit formula (`converse_explicit_formula`) concludes.
-/

      ∫ r, intervalPhaseKernel η a b r ∂boundaryMeasure hW := by

  haveI := sFinite_boundaryMeasure hW
  set g : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ := fun t r => η / (η ^ 2 + (r - t) ^ 2)
  have hg0 : ∀ t r, 0 ≤ g t r := fun t r => by dsimp [g]; positivity
  have hpt : ∀ t : ℝ,
      ENNReal.ofReal (weilContinuation hW (((1 / 2 + η : ℝ) : ℂ) + t * I)).re =
        ∫⁻ r, ENNReal.ofReal (g t r) ∂μ := by
    intro t
    simpa [g] using ofReal_re_weilContinuation_eq hW (1 / 2 + η) t (by linarith)
  have hre0 : ∀ t : ℝ,
      0 ≤ (weilContinuation hW (((1 / 2 + η : ℝ) : ℂ) + t * I)).re := fun t =>
    re_weilContinuation_nonneg hW (by simp; linarith)

    refine Complex.continuous_re.comp ?_
    exact (differentiableOn_weilContinuation hW).continuousOn.comp_continuous (by fun_prop)
      fun t => show (1 / 2 : ℝ) < (((1 / 2 + η : ℝ) : ℂ) + t * I).re by simp; linarith
  rw [integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae (Eventually.of_forall hre0)
    hcont.aestronglyMeasurable,
